title: Two sum
statement_markdown: Write a function `two_sum(nums: list[int], target: int) -> tuple[int, int]` that returns the indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`. You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice. The answer should be returned as a tuple of the two indices.

hints: A brute force solution takes O(n^2) time. Can you do it in O(n)?
Use a hash map (dictionary) to remember the values you have seen so far and their indices.
explanation: We can use a hash map to map the elements we've seen so far to their indices. As we iterate through the list, for each element we calculate its complement (target - num). If the complement is already in the hash map, we found our pair.
